understanding: Stage 1 adds durable per-camera scene memory to OKO without retraining the detector. The goal is to suppress false VLM wakeups on static cameras by learning background, normal object locations/classes, and durable static furniture track ids, then using that memory in the live VLM gate.
summary: Implement Stage 1 as small reviewed atoms: first create and test src/oko/memory/scene.py with durable SceneModel state under runs/scene/<camera_id>/; then persist static furniture evidence from events/builder.py; then integrate SceneModel into pipeline/live.py so VLM is skipped only when a detection matches durable furniture and shows near-zero motion against the learned background plate. Verification must run pytest from C:\Users\rafie\bridge-projects\oko after each assembled chapter.

decision_atoms.statement: Create src/oko/memory/scene.py as the only new core module for Stage 1 scene memory.
decision_atoms.reason: Keeps the learning logic isolated and testable before touching live pipeline behavior.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Initial integration is slightly slower because adapters are needed in existing files.

decision_atoms.statement: Persist SceneModel data under runs/scene/<camera_id>/ with separate files for metadata, background plate, normality grid, and furniture registry.
decision_atoms.reason: Separate durable artifacts reduce corruption risk and make partial updates easier to inspect and test.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: More files to manage than a single monolithic state file.

decision_atoms.statement: Use EMA as the default background plate update path, with optional median/bootstrap support if frame buffering already fits existing OKO patterns.
decision_atoms.reason: EMA is cheap, streaming-friendly, and suitable for live static cameras during warmup and maintenance.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: EMA can absorb slow-moving objects unless updates are gated by no-motion/no-moving-track conditions.

decision_atoms.statement: Only update the background plate on frames that have no moving tracks or otherwise pass a strict static-frame predicate.
decision_atoms.reason: The plate must represent the stable camera scene, not transient people or vehicles.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Sparse update opportunities can delay convergence on busy cameras.

decision_atoms.statement: Represent normality as a fixed 16x12 grid storing per-cell YOLO class statistics: count/persistence, confidence EMA, and last_seen timestamp.
decision_atoms.reason: This is simple, durable, explainable, and matches the requested spatial-normality behavior.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Coarse cells may miss fine object placement changes near cell boundaries.

decision_atoms.statement: Add durable furniture registry entries keyed by stable camera-local track/object identity where possible, with bbox/class/confidence/static evidence and timestamps.
decision_atoms.reason: The current _static_track_ids signal is useful but lost per event; durable evidence is needed to suppress repeated false positives.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Track ids may not be stable across process restarts, so registry matching must also support spatial/class similarity.

decision_atoms.statement: Modify events/builder.py minimally to expose or forward _static_track_ids to SceneModel instead of changing event semantics broadly.
decision_atoms.reason: This satisfies durability without destabilizing event construction behavior.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: The first implementation may need a small adapter if builder currently has no clean persistence hook.

decision_atoms.statement: Integrate SceneModel into pipeline/live.py at the VLM-gate decision point, not earlier in detector inference.
decision_atoms.reason: Stage 1 is suppression-only and must not change detection model outputs or training behavior.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Downstream code still sees detections unless the existing VLM gate owns suppression semantics.

decision_atoms.statement: Skip VLM only when both conditions are true: detection matches durable furniture/normality and motion against the background plate is approximately zero.
decision_atoms.reason: Combining semantic-spatial memory with pixel-level stillness avoids suppressing genuinely new or moved objects.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Requires threshold tuning for lighting changes and camera noise.

decision_atoms.statement: Implement a 2-5 minute warmup state where SceneModel learns but does not aggressively suppress until minimum evidence thresholds are met.
decision_atoms.reason: Prevents early false negatives from an undertrained scene memory.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: False positives may continue during warmup.

decision_atoms.statement: Decompose implementation into reviewable chapters and request architect review of atoms before assembling each chapter: scene module/tests, builder persistence/tests, live gate/tests, full project verification.
decision_atoms.reason: Matches the contract constraint and reduces risk in a high-risk pipeline change.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Adds coordination overhead before code assembly.

decision_atoms.statement: Run pytest from C:\Users\rafie\bridge-projects\oko as mandatory verification, plus focused tests for each atom where practical.
decision_atoms.reason: The contract explicitly requires project tests, not only bridge smoke checks.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Full tests may be slower and may expose unrelated existing failures that need triage.

assumptions: OKO already has a stable camera_id available in pipeline/live.py or a nearby runtime context.
runs/ is the accepted durable runtime-output root in the OKO project.
events/builder.py currently computes _static_track_ids before final event emission and can be minimally extended to expose that signal.
Frame data or a comparable image array is available at the VLM-gate point or can be passed there without broad pipeline refactoring.
Existing tests can be extended under the OKO project without changing external bridge tooling.
Architect review is a process gate for atom decomposition, not a requirement to call an unavailable tool from this proposal response.

risks.risk: Incorrect suppression could hide real incidents if furniture matching is too permissive.
risks.mitigation: Require both durable furniture/normality match and near-zero plate motion; use conservative thresholds and no aggressive suppression during warmup.

risks.risk: Background plate may learn transient objects on busy cameras.
risks.mitigation: Update plate only on frames with no moving tracks and add minimum stable-frame evidence before enabling suppression.

risks.risk: Track ids may not persist across restarts, making _static_track_ids alone insufficient.
risks.mitigation: Persist class, bbox/grid location, confidence, static duration, and timestamps so matching can fall back to spatial/class similarity.

risks.risk: Lighting changes, compression noise, or camera auto-exposure may look like motion.
risks.mitigation: Use normalized frame difference thresholds, small morphology/area filters if already available, and configurable tolerances.

risks.risk: Durable files under runs/scene may become corrupt after interrupted writes.
risks.mitigation: Use atomic write-rename for JSON/metadata and tolerate missing partial artifacts by rebuilding from warmup.

risks.risk: Pipeline/live.py integration may be tightly coupled to existing VLM-gate logic.
risks.mitigation: Keep integration as a narrow predicate/helper call with tests around the gate decision rather than refactoring the pipeline.

risks.risk: Full project pytest may fail for unrelated pre-existing reasons.
risks.mitigation: Record focused test results separately, capture full pytest failure details, and avoid masking unrelated failures.

minimal_version: Stage 1 MVP: new SceneModel module with durable JSON/NumPy artifacts, EMA background plate updated only on static frames, 16x12 normality grid, furniture registry ingestion from _static_track_ids, conservative warmup gating, and one live.py VLM-skip predicate requiring furniture match plus near-zero plate motion.
advanced_version: Stage 1 complete version: robust atomic persistence with schema versioning, median bootstrap plus EMA maintenance, restart-safe furniture matching by spatial/class similarity, configurable thresholds per camera, diagnostics for why VLM was skipped or allowed, and focused plus full pytest coverage in bridge-projects/oko.
